# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 45 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_045_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 12, Part 2 — The Angel of Luxury and the Angel of Punishment

**45:1** He said to me: "You know that you are a servant of God, and that you serve in his lordship, and that his power is great and incomprehensible, and that he made all things and made them out of nothing, and that he alone is able to contain all things but himself cannot be contained.

**45:2** Have faith therefore in him and fear him; and fearing him, be self-controlled. Keep these things and cast away from yourself all evil desire, and clothe yourself with every good and holy desire. For if you keep these commandments, you shall live to God."

**45:3** "Lord," I said, "strengthen me, for I have many distractions from the world and from the devil and from men who rule over the living and the dead and from those who are powerful here. For there are many diversions and they sweep me away." "I know," he said, "but I shall be with you and I shall deliver you from them all. But only keep my commandments and you will not be delivered up to them. But trust in God and he will deliver you."

**45:4** "I trust him, lord," I said. "And why do you not fear him?" he said. "Because you trust him." "Lord," I said, "your commandments are great and good and glorious and able to save the soul of a man. But if any man should know that he is able to keep these commandments, he will keep them; but if the heart of a man is very hard toward God and there is great weakness in him, then he despairs and says in his heart: these things are too hard to keep. His heart therefore becomes hard and he abandons the living God."

**45:5** "These thoughts are of the devil," he said, "who is an enemy of your Lord. Do not allow these thoughts to enter your heart, and do not doubt concerning these commandments, that you are not able to keep them. But remember rather him who is able to do all things and who makes all things possible, as he wills. On account of his great power and his great glory he can accomplish all these things. So trust and believe in God."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the dialogue structure and theological argument of Hermas.*
